description: MindGuard Manipulation Detection Scoring Rubric. Each category defines a class of psychological manipulation tactic, its weight in the final score, and example phrases for detection.

categories.description: Artificial time pressure used to bypass critical thinking and force impulsive action. Often creates a false sense of scarcity or deadline.
Exaggeration or fabrication of threats, dangers, or catastrophic outcomes to trigger the fear response and override rational decision-making.
Positioning information as suppressed, hidden, or censored by powerful actors to create an in-group vs. out-group dynamic and dismiss counter-evidence.
example_phrases: they don't want you to know

categories.description: Exaggerated, dramatic language designed to provoke strong emotional reactions and increase engagement, often at the expense of factual accuracy.
Use of emotionally charged language to trigger strong feelings (rage, grief, pride, disgust) that cloud objective evaluation of information.
Use of guilt, shame, or moral obligation to coerce action. Creates a false dichotomy where not acting is equated with moral failure or complicity.
Vague or false appeals to authority figures, experts, or institutions without verifiable citations. Often used to lend false credibility to claims.
Leveraging social conformity pressure by implying that a large majority already believes or acts in a certain way, making non-compliance seem abnormal.
High-pressure demands for immediate action, sharing, or engagement. Often used to spread content virally before critical evaluation can occur.
Use of extreme, unqualified absolute statements that leave no room for nuance, exceptions, or uncertainty. A hallmark of black-and-white thinking.
Presenting claims as factual while using vague qualifiers that signal the absence of actual evidence. Allows false claims to evade fact-checking.

dimensions.name: Sender & Domain Legitimacy
dimensions.description: Is the sender domain legitimate? Does it match the claimed organisation?

scoring_guide.0-20: Verified sender from known legitimate domain (e.g. onlinesbi.com, google.com)
scoring_guide.21-40: Plausible sender, minor domain mismatch or unknown sender
scoring_guide.41-60: Suspicious sender, generic domain (gmail for a bank claim), slight mismatch
scoring_guide.81-100: Clear impersonation — domain has no relation to claimed sender

red_flags: Hyphenated brand names in domain (sbi-secure, paypal-verify)
Country TLD mismatch (.ru, .info, .net for banks)
Free email service for official communications (gmail, yahoo for banks)
Misspelled brand name in domain
Subdomain spoofing (paypal.attacker.com)

dimensions.name: Artificial Urgency & Time Pressure
dimensions.description: Does the email use artificial deadlines or urgency to pressure the reader?

scoring_guide.0-20: No time pressure; informational or casual tone
scoring_guide.21-40: Mild reminder with genuine deadline (trial expiry, appointment)
scoring_guide.41-60: Moderate urgency; some pressure but plausibly legitimate
scoring_guide.61-80: Strong artificial urgency; '24-hour' or 'today only' threats
scoring_guide.81-100: Extreme urgency designed to prevent rational thinking (1-hour deadline, immediate action)

red_flags: Deadlines under 48 hours for serious account actions
All-caps urgency words (URGENT, IMMEDIATE, ACT NOW)
Countdown language without verifiable basis
Consequences escalate rapidly (suspension → permanent closure → arrest)

dimensions.name: Threats & Fear Induction
dimensions.description: Does the email use threats of financial loss, account closure, legal action, or arrest?

scoring_guide.0-20: No threats; neutral or positive framing
scoring_guide.21-40: Mild consequence mentioned (account revert to free tier, late fee)
scoring_guide.61-80: Strong threat (account closure, funds held, data deletion)
scoring_guide.81-100: Extreme threat (arrest, legal action, CBI/police involvement)

red_flags: Arrest or legal action threats
Fund freezing or permanent account closure
Threats that escalate if you contact others (secrecy demand)
Aadhaar/PAN/government ID linked to illegal activity claims

dimensions.name: Credential or Payment Request
dimensions.description: Does the email request passwords, OTPs, card details, bank details, or payments?

scoring_guide.0-20: No request for sensitive info or payment
scoring_guide.21-40: Requests non-sensitive info (name, address for delivery)
scoring_guide.41-60: Requests account verification via legitimate-looking portal
scoring_guide.61-80: Requests OTP, password, or partial card/bank details
scoring_guide.81-100: Requests full credentials, card numbers, bank account + IFSC, or upfront payment

red_flags: Requesting OTP via email (legitimate services never do this)
KYC update via external link
Wire transfer request with secrecy demand (BEC pattern)
Advance fee payment to claim prize or refund
Full bank account + IFSC for 'refund processing'

dimensions.name: Link & URL Suspicious Indicators
dimensions.description: Are links in the email suspicious, shortened, or leading to non-official domains?

scoring_guide.0-20: Official domain links or no links
scoring_guide.41-60: Shortened URLs (bit.ly) or links not matching sender's brand
scoring_guide.61-80: Lookalike domains or mismatched anchor text vs URL
scoring_guide.81-100: Clear phishing domains, IP-based links, or .ru/.info for financial services

red_flags: Anchor text says 'Click here' but URL is external domain
Shortened URLs in financial or account security emails
HTTP (not HTTPS) links for login pages
IP address as URL
Mismatched TLD for claimed brand

dimensions.name: Social Engineering & Manipulation Tactics
dimensions.description: Does the email use authority, reciprocity, social proof, or other psychological manipulation?

scoring_guide.41-60: Moderate manipulation (authority appeal, fake social proof)
scoring_guide.61-80: Strong manipulation (impersonation of authority, conspiracy framing)
scoring_guide.81-100: Multiple stacked tactics: authority + urgency + fear + secrecy

red_flags: CEO/boss impersonation with secrecy demand (BEC)
Government authority impersonation (CBI, IT Department, RBI)
Conspiracy framing ('what banks/doctors don't want you to know')
Fake testimonials or inflated social proof numbers
Secrecy/confidentiality demand to prevent victim from seeking help

india_specific_patterns.description: High-priority patterns specific to Indian email threat landscape
patterns: KYC update requests claiming to be from SBI, HDFC, ICICI, Axis
Aadhaar linked to illegal activity threats
CBI, ED, Cyber Crime Cell impersonation
